From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@novamed.com>

Subject: RFI: Hosted API - Data handling & purge

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this RFI. As part of our procurement checklist we need written answers to a few items specific to your hosted API behavior around data residency, retention and deletion. We're particularly focused on: primary/replica location guarantees, timeline for customer-initiated erasure (including backups), caching/KV cache eviction, and the audit evidence you provide after a deletion request.

Can you confirm the following (short answers are fine, we may follow up):
- Where does customer data reside by default and can it be pinned to a US-only region?
- After a tenant requests data deletion, what are the steps and expected completion windows for: primary store, KV cache, logs, and backups?
- Do you provide a deletion certificate or job ID that we can retain?
- Retention policy for diagnostic logs and request traces (by default, and for paid retention add-ons).

Please attach any short fact sheet or timeline you already have. Procurement will want an estimate of when we can see the certificate after an erasure request.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Patel
Director, Information Security
NovaMed Health

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below and I attached a compact fact sheet + timeline CSV for your SOC/Procurement pack. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if you'd like more detail.

- Residency: By default tenant data is colocated to one region; for NovaMed we can pin all inference storage and backups to the us-west-2 region (contractually supported via a Regional Addendum).

- Erasure timeline (customer-initiated):
  * Primary data store: deletion job triggered immediately; data removed from live store within 24–72 hours depending on active writes and in-flight batches.
  * KV/prefix caches: invalidated within 24 hours; active in-memory caches are evicted on next access and we proactively flush relevant keys within the window.
  * Request traces / structured logs: default retention 90 days; on erasure request we scrub PII within 72 hours and mark traces for redaction.
  * Backups & snapshots: backups are retained for up to 90 days by default. For deletions we schedule a backup rotation and physical overwrite; tombstone removal and final overwrite complete within 90–120 days depending on backup retention windows.

- Deletion certificate / job ID: yes — we return a Data Erasure Job ID and a signed PDF certificate once the primary deletion and cache invalidation complete. Backup overwrite attestations are provided as a follow-up within the backup retention window.

- Logs & traces retention: default 90 days. We offer paid retention tiers (180/365 days) and can set retention exceptions in the contract. Audit logs (admin actions) are retained 1 year by default and available via the console/export API.

Attached: HostedAPI_Data_Handling_Fact_Sheet.pdf; Retention_Timeline.csv

Next steps: if this satisfies Procurement, we can convert the answers into the RFI spreadsheet and generate an initial erasure-run example for you to review.

— Soojin

1) Can you confirm the backup overwrite process is irreversible and whether snapshots are stored encrypted with customer-specific keys? What is the typical time between a deletion request and the "attestation" you provide for backup overwrite?

2) For request traces that contain PII (chat transcripts, prompts), when you say "scrub PII within 72 hours" — do you do a redaction in place or a full deletion from the trace store? We need to understand residual inference artifacts (embeddings, prompt fragments).

3) If we require an accelerated purge for a regulated workflow (e.g., 30-day full purge SLA including backups), can you support that as a paid SLA? If so, what's the lead time and cost ballpark?

Sara — quick technical follow-up and blown-out answers to your three points. Quoting the specific asks below, then our operational response.

> 1) Backup overwrite irreversibility & keys / attestation timeline

- Encryption: snapshots and backups are encrypted at rest using customer-scoped KMS keys when requested; by default we use tenant-specific envelope keys with separation between control-plane metadata and payload encryption. Key lifecycle (rotate/revoke) is handled via KMS integration and documented in the fact sheet.
- Overwrite: backups live on immutable snapshot schedules for N days (N = configured retention). After a deletion request we mark the tenant snapshots for expedited rotation and schedule zeroing/overwrite of backup volumes. Immutable cloud snapshots (where supported) are retired and replaced by new snapshots that exclude the tenant. The physical overwrite process depends on the underlying provider; we ensure cryptographic disposal by deleting the encryption key for the snapshot where customer-managed keys are used, which renders the snapshot unreadable.
- Attestation timeline: Data Erasure Job ID is emitted within 24–72 hours for primary-store and cache actions. Backup overwrite attestations are provided as a secondary certificate once the snapshot overwrite job completes — typically within the configured retention window (we can supply an SLA for accelerated jobs as a paid addendum).

> 2) Traces and PII in request logs / embeddings

- Approach: we separate structured request metadata (timestamps, response latencies) from payloads (prompts, responses, embeddings). For payloads, our hosted API offers two controls: ephemeral mode (default for many customers) where prompt/response payloads are not logged beyond transient processing, and persistent mode where payloads are written to a tenant-scoped object store for debugging / eval purposes.
- Erasure: for persistent-mode payloads we perform full deletion of the objects on erasure requests (not just redaction). Embeddings derived from user data are tracked via an index; when a deletion request is received we enqueue index reconciliation jobs that identify and delete related embedding vectors. Index reconciliation completes within the same primary deletion window (24–72 hours) for active indexes; older cold backups follow the backup overwrite schedule.

> 3) Accelerated purge SLA (30-day full purge)

- Yes — we offer an accelerated purge SLA as a contractual add-on. Requirements: 1) tenant data pinned to a single region and 2) customer-managed encryption keys (recommended). Lead time: 2–4 weeks to provision the accelerated retention/config and test. Cost: quoted per TB of retained backup data and an initial provisioning fee; ballpark: $6k–$12k per TB one-time plus ongoing per-month premium. Exact pricing depends on dataset size and snapshot frequency.

Additional items:
- Evidence model: Data Erasure Job ID + a PDF certificate for primary deletion (within 72 hours) + a secondary backup overwrite attest when that job completes. We persist audit logs of the erasure operation in the console (admin-only access) for one year by default.
- Example API response: we can share a sample JSON payload for the erasure response (Job ID + status + timestamps). I'll attach a template certificate and an example job response to the Hub Drive.

If these answers work, Soojin and I can produce a short insert for your legal/IT security pack and a sample API call that you can run in our sandbox.

— Jonas
